title: Passive traffic tap pipeline for non-invasive model evaluation and cost shepherding
creator: Priya Shah
description: Build a passive traffic-tap pipeline that captures a stratified sample of live requests and delivers them to sandboxed model runtimes for evaluation without increasing production token spend or impacting live latency. The tap must provide per-tenant budget accounting, strong tenancy isolation, privacy-preserving redaction, and an observable feedback loop (quality metrics + diffing against production outputs) that can drive automated rollback decisions.
background: We need to continuously evaluate candidate model versions and rollout strategies (canaries, A/B tests) against real traffic to detect regressions. Existing approaches (inline duplication / synchronous forks) increase GPU cost and risk interfering with production latency. Prior work in the repo focuses on budgeted sampling and quarantine, but we lack a non-invasive, tenant-aware tap that integrates cost fencing and auto-rollback signals.
decision_log: Decision: prefer asynchronous tap with selective payload materialization over inline synchronous duplication to eliminate added tail latency and avoid double-counting production tokens. Use stratified reservoir sampling by tenant and request type to preserve representativeness while capping cost. Store minimal request context (prefix hashes, metadata) rather than full PII content; implement redaction hooks per customer policy. Record full decision rationale and alternatives evaluated in Drive (link below).
implementation_plan: 1) Proxy hook: add non-blocking tap to edge proxy to emit compact event to tap queue (gRPC/HTTP) with sampling metadata.
2) Sampling engine: implement stratified sampling service that enforces per-tenant token and event budgets; supports reservoir and deterministic hashing for reproducible selection.
3) Materializer: ephemeral worker pool that reconstructs sandboxable payloads with redaction, truncation, and annotation (do not include secrets or user tokens).
4) Sandbox runtime: route materialized requests to dedicated sandbox inference pool (can reuse smaller quantized variants) with tenant isolation via namespaces and ephemeral KV caches.
5) Scoring & diffing: compute similarity metrics (log-prob deltas, token-level diffs, structured output checks) and surface regressions to the console and rollback engine.
6) Cost & quarantine controls: implement per-tenant budget thresholds, soft-throttles + quarantine mode when budgets are exhausted; surface cost estimates in Console.
7) Auto-rollback integration: wire regression detector to rollout controller with configurable thresholds and cooldowns.
8) Telemetry & tracing: ensure end-to-end trace correlation and sampling provenance metadata for investigations.
9) Security review & retention: run security review, ensure retention TTLs and KMS encryption for persisted artifacts.
10) Pilot: run with 3 internal tenants, evaluate representativeness and cost, iterate on sampling parameters.
11) Production roll: flip opt-in default for self-serve customers after pilot + documentation.
acceptance_criteria: Tap emits <=1% additional end-to-end latency to production 99th percentile (async path must be non-blocking).
Representative sampling: captured request distribution by tenant and endpoint within 5% of baseline per-week traffic composition for pilot tenants.
Per-tenant daily token cost for sandbox traffic is bounded by configured budget; when budget is exhausted sandbox requests are skipped and metric emitted.
Sandboxed model outputs are stored redacted and encrypted with TTL; no production secrets are present in persisted artifacts.
Automatic rollback trigger fires during pilot on injected regression signal and successfully pauses canary rollout in staged environment.
Console shows tap-derived quality deltas and cost estimates per-tenant and per-model.
Security review completed and signed off by InfoSec.
End-to-end tests for sampling determinism, budget fencing, and quarantine behavior in CI.
Documentation and runbook for incidents and false-positive rollback cases.
Pilot run completes with cost <= projected estimates and produces at least one actionable regression finding.
risks: Sampling bias for low-volume tenants may miss regressions — mitigated via minimum sample quotas and synthetic augmentation.
Incorrect redaction could leak PII — mitigate with explicit redact rules and security review.
Sandbox runtime cost could grow if sampling parameters are too permissive — mitigate with hard budget fences and automated quarantine.
Session-coherent features (KV cache warmness) are hard to reproduce; sandbox runs may produce false negatives for cache-sensitive regressions.
Auto-rollback false positives might interrupt healthy rollouts — implement cooldowns, human-in-the-loop confirmation for high-impact rollouts.
Operational complexity: more moving parts in telemetry pipeline increases SRE burden; require runbooks and alerts.
Legal/regulatory constraints for certain customers may prohibit tap usage — opt-out and per-customer gating required.
testing_plan: Unit tests for sampling engine, deterministic hashing, and budget enforcement.
Integration tests: end-to-end tap from edge -> materializer -> sandbox with trace correlation.
Chaos tests: simulate backlog and ensure tap is backpressure-safe and does not affect production proxies.
Cost simulation: run replay on historical traffic to estimate daily token spend across tenant percentiles.
Pilot with internal teams then with 3 external low-risk tenants before broader opt-in.
Rollback drill: simulate regression signal and validate automated rollback + manual override path.
Security testing: redaction fuzzing and code review by InfoSec.
SLO tests: verify async non-blocking guarantees under 95th/99th percentile proxy load.
